name: Lanthanum strontium cuprate, close to optimal doping
equilibrium_context: Tc about 37 K, superconductor with a clear Josephson plasma resonance
summary: Artifact warning. The methodologically most important negative entry in this area.

driven_states.emergent_property: Intense near-infrared excitation in the superconducting state produces a red shift of the Josephson plasma resonance that persists over hundreds of picoseconds - that is, destruction rather than creation of c-axis coherence. The metastable spectral features can be explained by photoinduced surface heating.
driven_states.caveat: The value lies in the methodological warning: the customary two-layer reconstruction (transformed surface layer above unchanged bulk), on which practically all positive cuprate findings rest, can generate artifacts in the non-equilibrium response. The finding does not refute light-induced superconductivity in other compounds, but it raises the burden of proof.
driven_states.measured_quantity: Josephson plasma resonance in the c-axis reflectivity
